import Mathlib

namespace SignlessLaplacianNonUniq

open Matrix SimpleGraph

/-- The signless Laplacian `Q(G) = D(G) + A(G)` of a finite simple graph on `Fin n`,
as a real matrix. -/
noncomputable def signlessLaplacian {n : ℕ} (G : SimpleGraph (Fin n)) [DecidableRel G.Adj] :
    Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ :=
  Matrix.diagonal (fun v => (G.degree v : ℝ)) + G.adjMatrix ℝ

/-- The signless Laplacian spectral radius: the supremum of the real eigenvalues.
For a real symmetric matrix (such as any `signlessLaplacian G`) this is the largest
eigenvalue. -/
noncomputable def QSpecRad {n : ℕ} (Q : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ) : ℝ :=
  sSup {μ : ℝ | ∃ v : Fin n → ℝ, v ≠ 0 ∧ Q.mulVec v = μ • v}

/-- The self dot product of a nonzero real vector is strictly positive. -/
lemma dotProduct_self_pos {n : ℕ} {v : Fin n → ℝ} (h : v ≠ 0) : 0 < v ⬝ᵥ v := by
  rcases Function.ne_iff.1 h with ⟨i, hi⟩
  refine Finset.sum_pos' (fun k _ => mul_self_nonneg (v k)) ⟨i, Finset.mem_univ i, ?_⟩
  have := mul_self_pos.2 hi; simpa using this

/-- **Spectral-radius criterion.** If `c` is realised by an eigenvector and the
Rayleigh quotient of `Q` is bounded above by `c` (equivalently `Q ⪯ c • I`), then the
signless-Laplacian-style spectral radius `QSpecRad Q` equals `c`. -/
lemma QSpecRad_eq {n : ℕ} (Q : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ) (c : ℝ)
    (hev : ∃ v : Fin n → ℝ, v ≠ 0 ∧ Q.mulVec v = c • v)
    (hray : ∀ v : Fin n → ℝ, v ⬝ᵥ Q.mulVec v ≤ c * (v ⬝ᵥ v)) :
    QSpecRad Q = c := by
  apply IsGreatest.csSup_eq
  refine ⟨hev, ?_⟩
  rintro μ ⟨v, hv, hqv⟩
  have h1 : v ⬝ᵥ Q.mulVec v = μ * (v ⬝ᵥ v) := by rw [hqv, dotProduct_smul, smul_eq_mul]

  have h3 := hray v
  rw [h1] at h3
  exact le_of_mul_le_mul_right (by linarith) h2

def NoTwoDisjointK4 {n : ℕ} (G : SimpleGraph (Fin n)) : Prop :=
  ¬ ∃ s t : Finset (Fin n), G.IsNClique 4 s ∧ G.IsNClique 4 t ∧ Disjoint s t

  Adj i j := i ≠ j ∧ (i.val < 3 ∨ j.val < 3)
  symm := fun _ _ ⟨h1, h2⟩ => ⟨h1.symm, h2.symm⟩
  loopless := ⟨fun _ h => h.1 rfl⟩

instance : DecidableRel Gjoin.Adj := fun i j => by unfold Gjoin; infer_instance

lemma sljoin_apply (i j : Fin 9) :
    signlessLaplacian Gjoin i j
      = (if i = j then (if i.val < 3 then (8:ℝ) else 3) else 0) + (if Gjoin.Adj i j then 1 else 0) := by
  have hd : ∀ k : Fin 9, Gjoin.degree k = (if k.val < 3 then 8 else 3) := by decide
  simp only [signlessLaplacian, Matrix.add_apply, Matrix.diagonal_apply,
    SimpleGraph.adjMatrix_apply, hd]
  split <;> simp_all

/-- The block vector `(3,3,3,1,1,1,1,1,1)` is an eigenvector of `Q(K₃ ∨ \overline{K₆})`
with eigenvalue `12`. -/
def vjoin : Fin 9 → ℝ := fun i => if i.val < 3 then 3 else 1

lemma join_eigenvector : (signlessLaplacian Gjoin).mulVec vjoin = (12:ℝ) • vjoin := by
  funext i
  rw [Matrix.mulVec]
  show dotProduct (signlessLaplacian Gjoin i) vjoin = _
  simp only [dotProduct, sljoin_apply, Fin.sum_univ_succ, Fin.sum_univ_zero, Fin.reduceSucc,
    vjoin, Pi.smul_apply, smul_eq_mul]
  fin_cases i <;> · norm_num [Gjoin, Fin.ext_iff]

/-- Rayleigh upper bound `x ⬝ Qx ≤ 12 (x ⬝ x)` for `Q(K₃ ∨ \overline{K₆})`; equivalently
`Q(K₃ ∨ \overline{K₆}) ⪯ 12 • I`.  Proved by an explicit sum-of-squares certificate. -/
lemma join_rayleigh (v : Fin 9 → ℝ) :
    v ⬝ᵥ (signlessLaplacian Gjoin).mulVec v ≤ 12 * (v ⬝ᵥ v) := by
  simp only [dotProduct, Matrix.mulVec, sljoin_apply, Fin.sum_univ_succ, Fin.sum_univ_zero,
    Fin.reduceSucc]
  norm_num [Gjoin, Fin.ext_iff]
  nlinarith [sq_nonneg (v 0 - v 1), sq_nonneg (v 0 - v 2), sq_nonneg (v 1 - v 2),
    sq_nonneg (v 3 - v 4), sq_nonneg (v 3 - v 5), sq_nonneg (v 3 - v 6), sq_nonneg (v 3 - v 7),
    sq_nonneg (v 3 - v 8), sq_nonneg (v 4 - v 5), sq_nonneg (v 4 - v 6), sq_nonneg (v 4 - v 7),
    sq_nonneg (v 4 - v 8), sq_nonneg (v 5 - v 6), sq_nonneg (v 5 - v 7), sq_nonneg (v 5 - v 8),
    sq_nonneg (v 6 - v 7), sq_nonneg (v 6 - v 8), sq_nonneg (v 7 - v 8),
    sq_nonneg (2 * (v 0 + v 1 + v 2) - 3 * (v 3 + v 4 + v 5 + v 6 + v 7 + v 8))]

/-- Any `4`-clique of `K₃ ∨ \overline{K₆}` has at least `3` vertices in the universal
part `{0,1,2}` (the independent part contributes at most one vertex to any clique). -/
lemma join_clique_lo_card {s : Finset (Fin 9)} (hs : Gjoin.IsNClique 4 s) :
    3 ≤ (s.filter (fun x => x.val < 3)).card := by
  have hcard : s.card = 4 := hs.2
  have hhi : (s.filter (fun x => ¬ x.val < 3)).card ≤ 1 := by
    by_contra h
    push_neg at h
    obtain ⟨x, hx, y, hy, hxy⟩ := Finset.one_lt_card.1 h
    simp only [Finset.mem_filter] at hx hy
    have hadj := hs.1 hx.1 hy.1 hxy
    rcases hadj.2 with h3 | h3 <;> omega
  have hsplit := Finset.card_filter_add_card_filter_not (s := s) (fun x => x.val < 3)
  omega

/-- `K₃ ∨ \overline{K₆}` is `2K₄`-free: two disjoint `K₄`'s would need `≥ 6` vertices
inside the `3`-element universal part. -/
theorem gjoin_noTwoDisjointK4 : NoTwoDisjointK4 Gjoin := by
  rintro ⟨s, t, hs, ht, hdisj⟩
  have hs3 := join_clique_lo_card hs
  have ht3 := join_clique_lo_card ht
  set Cs := s.filter (fun x => x.val < 3) with hCs
  set Ct := t.filter (fun x => x.val < 3) with hCt
  have hsub : Cs ∪ Ct ⊆ Finset.univ.filter (fun x : Fin 9 => x.val < 3) := by
    intro x hx
    simp only [Finset.mem_union, hCs, hCt, Finset.mem_filter] at hx ⊢
    rcases hx with h | h <;> exact ⟨Finset.mem_univ _, h.2⟩
  have hcard3 : (Finset.univ.filter (fun x : Fin 9 => x.val < 3)).card = 3 := by decide
  have hdisj2 : Disjoint Cs Ct := Finset.disjoint_filter_filter hdisj
  have hunion : (Cs ∪ Ct).card = Cs.card + Ct.card := Finset.card_union_of_disjoint hdisj2
  have := Finset.card_le_card hsub
  omega

/-! ### The two graphs are not isomorphic. -/

/-- `K_{3,3,3}` and `K₃ ∨ \overline{K₆}` are not isomorphic: the latter has a
universal vertex (vertex `0`), while the former has none (it is `6`-regular). -/
theorem gtri_not_iso_gjoin : IsEmpty (Gtri ≃g Gjoin) := by
  rw [isEmpty_iff]
  intro φ
  have gtri_nouniv : ∀ u : Fin 9, ∃ w, w ≠ u ∧ ¬ Gtri.Adj u w := by decide
  obtain ⟨w, hw, hnadj⟩ := gtri_nouniv (φ.symm 0)
  apply hnadj
  have h0 : Gjoin.Adj 0 (φ w) := by
    refine ⟨?_, Or.inl (by norm_num)⟩
    intro hcontra
    apply hw
    have : φ w = φ (φ.symm 0) := by rw [hcontra]; simp
    exact φ.injective this
  have hstep : Gjoin.Adj (φ (φ.symm 0)) (φ w) := by simpa using h0
  exact (φ.map_adj_iff).1 hstep

/-! ### Main results. -/

/-- **Main Theorem 1.** The signless Laplacian spectral radius of `K_{3,3,3} = T₃(9)`
is exactly `12`. -/
theorem QSpecRad_Gtri : QSpecRad (signlessLaplacian Gtri) = 12 := by
  refine QSpecRad_eq _ 12 ⟨fun _ => (1:ℝ), ?_, tri_eigenvector⟩ tri_rayleigh
  intro h
  have : (fun _ => (1:ℝ)) (0 : Fin 9) = 0 := by rw [h]; rfl
  simp at this

/-- **Main Theorem 2.** The signless Laplacian spectral radius of
`K₃ ∨ \overline{K₆} = K_{6,1,1,1}` is exactly `12`. -/
theorem QSpecRad_Gjoin : QSpecRad (signlessLaplacian Gjoin) = 12 := by
  refine QSpecRad_eq _ 12 ⟨vjoin, ?_, join_eigenvector⟩ join_rayleigh
  intro h
  have : vjoin 0 = 0 := by rw [h]; rfl
  simp [vjoin] at this

/-- **Main Theorem 3 (non-uniqueness / synthesis).** There exist two non-isomorphic
`2K₄`-free graphs on `9` vertices with identical signless Laplacian spectral radius.
Consequently the signless Laplacian spectral radius does not determine a `2K₄`-free
graph of order `9` up to isomorphism. -/
theorem signless_laplacian_spectral_radius_not_unique :
    ∃ G H : SimpleGraph (Fin 9), ∃ _ : DecidableRel G.Adj, ∃ _ : DecidableRel H.Adj,
      NoTwoDisjointK4 G ∧ NoTwoDisjointK4 H ∧ IsEmpty (G ≃g H) ∧
      QSpecRad (signlessLaplacian G) = QSpecRad (signlessLaplacian H) := by
  refine ⟨Gtri, Gjoin, inferInstance, inferInstance, gtri_noTwoDisjointK4,
    gjoin_noTwoDisjointK4, gtri_not_iso_gjoin, ?_⟩
  rw [QSpecRad_Gtri, QSpecRad_Gjoin]

end SignlessLaplacianNonUniq

# Computational Evidence — signless Laplacian spectral radius of 2K₄-free graphs on 9 vertices

All graphs are on `n = 9` vertices. The signless Laplacian is `Q(G) = D(G) + A(G)`
(degree diagonal plus adjacency). "Spectral radius" is the largest eigenvalue of `Q`,
computed below by exact rational arithmetic (checking `det(λI − Q) = 0`) and by
floating-point power iteration.

## 1. The motivating graph is *not* the maximiser at n = 9

`K₁ ∨ T₃(8) = K_{1,3,3,2}` (the claimed extremal graph) has

    ρ_Q(K_{1,3,3,2}) ≈ 13.14245736 .

Scanning **all** complete multipartite graphs on 9 vertices that are 2K₄-free and
computing `ρ_Q`, the top of the table is:

| partition (parts of the complete multipartite graph) | ρ_Q      | 2K₄-free? |
|------------------------------------------------------|----------|-----------|
| `[4,1,1,1,1,1]`  = `K₅ ∨ \overline{K₄}`              | 14.17891 | yes       |
| `[3,3,1,1,1]`                                        | 13.77200 | yes       |
| `[4,2,1,1,1]`                                        | 13.63787 | yes       |
| `[5,1,1,1,1]`                                        | 13.17891 | yes       |
| `[3,3,2,1]`      = `K₁ ∨ T₃(8) = K_{1,3,3,2}`        | 13.14246 | yes       |
| `[4,2,2,1]`                                          | 13.00000 | yes       |
| ...                                                  | ...      | ...       |
| `[6,1,1,1]`      = `K₃ ∨ \overline{K₆}`              | 12.00000 | yes       |
| `[3,3,3]`        = `T₃(9)`                            | 12.00000 | yes (K₄-free) |

So `K₅ ∨ \overline{K₄}` (spectral radius ≈ 14.18) strictly beats `K₁ ∨ T₃(8)`
(≈ 13.14). The reason is structural: a graph with no two disjoint `K₄` can be built
by putting a `K₄`-transversal of size `≤ 3` on top of an independent set. `K₅` uses
`≥ 3` clique vertices per `K₄`, so `K₅ ∨ \overline{K₄}` is 2K₄-free, and at the small
order `n = 9` this "concentrated" graph outperforms the "spread-out" Turán-type
`K₁ ∨ T₃(8)`. Hence the literal premise — that `K₁ ∨ T₃(8)` is *the* (non-unique)
maximiser — is **false** at `n = 9`; it is not a maximiser at all.

## 2. A genuine spectral-radius coincidence at the value 12

Two non-isomorphic 2K₄-free graphs share the *exact* value `12`:

* `K_{3,3,3} = T₃(9)`: it is `6`-regular, so `Q = 6I + A` and
  `ρ_Q = 6 + ρ_A = 6 + 6 = 12` exactly. (It is even `K₄`-free.)
* `K₃ ∨ \overline{K₆} = K_{6,1,1,1}`: quotient (equitable-partition) matrix
  `[[10,6],[3,3]]` on the (clique, independent) blocks has eigenvalues `12` and `1`;
  `12` is the Perron value. Eigenvector `(3,3,3,1,1,1,1,1,1)` verifies `Qv = 12v`.

Exact check (`det(12·I − Q) = 0`):

    K_{3,3,3}  :  12 is an eigenvalue  = True
    K_{6,1,1,1}:  12 is an eigenvalue  = True

These two graphs are **not** cospectral — only their leading eigenvalue agrees; their
degree sequences differ (`6⁹` versus `8³3⁶`), their edge counts differ (`27` versus
`21`), and their full `Q`-spectra differ. This is exactly the phenomenon formalised
in `NonUniqueness.lean`: the signless Laplacian spectral radius does **not** determine
a 2K₄-free graph of order `9` up to isomorphism.

## 3. Method notes

* `ρ_Q` values obtained by power iteration (2000–5000 iterations) and cross-checked
  for the value `12` by exact Gaussian elimination over `ℚ` on `12·I − Q`.
* 2K₄-freeness of each candidate checked by enumerating all `4`-cliques and testing
  for a disjoint pair.
* No OEIS sequence is relevant here (the object is a single small extremal
  comparison, not an integer sequence).

## 4. What the Lean development proves (0 sorries, standard axioms only)

* `QSpecRad_Gtri  : QSpecRad (signlessLaplacian Gtri)  = 12`
* `QSpecRad_Gjoin : QSpecRad (signlessLaplacian Gjoin) = 12`
* `gtri_noTwoDisjointK4`, `gjoin_noTwoDisjointK4` — both graphs are 2K₄-free
* `gtri_not_iso_gjoin` — the two graphs are not isomorphic
* `signless_laplacian_spectral_radius_not_unique` — the packaged non-uniqueness result
